en: The *Vajraśekhara-sūtra-uddhṛta-laghu-japa-anuṣṭhāna-vidhi*, also titled the *Pañcāṅga-laghu-japa-āvaśyaka-prayoga*,
in one fascicle.
Compiled by [the monk] Sù, who held the rank of Kaifǔ Yítóng Sī Tèjìn Shì Hónglú Qīng.
I prostrate to the one of unimpeded wisdom, the son born from the intention of the Secret Teaching;
relying upon that sūtra, I shall here collect these methods for practice.
A practitioner of the mantra path should first abide in the vow of equanimity.
With both the secret speech and the secret body, one subsequently performs the corresponding practice.
The samaya mantra is as follows:
the mudrā consists of joining the palms together and extending both thumbs upward.
At the five locations— the crown, shoulders, and heart— finally adding the position of the throat;
next, with the Immovable One, one clears away obstacles and removes impurities,
thereby purifying all matters, while binding and protecting in accordance with the appropriate rites.
The mantra of Acala is as follows:
Place the syllable for space (A) upon earth (La) and water (Va); place wind (Ya) and fire (Ra) vertically at the heart.
The sword of wisdom is likewise; drawn from its scabbard, it can accomplish all tasks.
Next, the Tathāgata Hook is taught for the purpose of inviting the tutelary deity;
all the lords of the assembly of holy ones shall come according to their original vows.
The mantra of the Tathāgata Hook is as follows:
The inner aspects of *śamatha* and *vipaśyanā* are crossed; firmly joined, the wind of wisdom stands erect.
Just slightly bent at its initial portion, the remaining wheels are shaped like rings.
By the power of the compassionate vows of Āryadeva, he descends in response to every invocation.
Present the samaya offerings; the mantras and mudrās are as previously explained.
Having manifested one’s fundamental vow, generate joy without error.
Next, according to one's capacity, perform offerings to express sincerity of heart.
With argha, incense, food, and lamps— down to even a single flower or a drop of water—
or even by merely directing the mind in visualization, the merit is supreme and most difficult to measure.
One should employ the common mudrās, adding them together with the secret mantras.
Both the manifest (*vijñapti*) and the unmanifest (*avijñapti*) are simultaneously accomplished.
The Universal Mantra is as follows:
Interlace the fingers of the Wisdom and Meditation hands, joining them level with the crown of the head.
With a mind that pervades everywhere, whatever is contemplated appears before one.
Having already performed the offerings, one should practice the constant recitation;
first donning the vajra armor, one performs the binding and protection in accordance with the ritual requirements.
The Mantra of the Vajra Armor:
First, join the palms with hollowed centers; interlace the wind-wheels (the little fingers) while holding the fire-wheels (the ring fingers);
let the great space-wheels (the thumbs) rest upon the base of the fire-wheels; finally, touch everywhere and place [the hands] at the heart.
Next, bind the boundaries of the cardinal and intermediate directions:
as before, with the Immovable One (*Acala*), turn counter-clockwise to perform the expulsion;
then rotate clockwise for the upper and lower directions, thoroughly touching all parts of the body. Thus the protective bonds are made entirely firm.
The mantras and their fundamental mudrās have already been distinguished as before.
Once the preparations are complete, one should display the fundamental mudrā;
adding it again to the five positions, one should perform it seven times or twice more.
Forming the mudrā of scattering above the crown,
with the body in half-lotus posture and mind composed, or sitting in the appropriate cross-legged position as taught according to the respective direction;
standing facing forward before the body, one beholds the image of a single, perfectly luminous orb.
Pure and without blemish, like the orb of the full moon, within which is the form of the central deity;
its color transcends the three realms, and its body is adorned with garments of exquisite fine silk;
a jeweled crown sits upon his head, from which dark blue hair flows down.
In the samādhi of profound stillness, A radiant blaze surpasses all lightning;
Just as within a pure mirror, The hidden and deep appear as true forms,
Revealing expressions of joy or anger, And manifesting conduct in accordance with one's vows.
The body is in accord with meditative absorption, the mind is lucid and undisturbed;
possessing the essence of the signless pure dharma, one responds to vows to deliver all sentient beings.
With focused concentration, one maintains mindfulness and recitation; once the prescribed number of counts has been completed, [the practice is finished].
When exhaustion has finally subsided,
one should reverently offer prayers and the like, and with earnest devotion, prostrate to the Sublime One.
Turning counter-clockwise without force, one releases the previously established protection.
Return and present the mudrā of the Honored One, opening it above the crown of the head.
Send the mind to the Holy Deity, prostrating with the five limbs touching the ground.
Then arise and follow the assembly in their virtuous practice; at the subsequent gathering, resume as before.
At times with two or three, or sometimes four, it is all like this.
Others circumambulate the stūpa, bathe the image, and praise the Vaipulya sūtras;
they adorn maṇḍalas and scatter flowers while praising the Buddha’s virtues.
Alternatively, being free from discursive thoughts and focusing single-mindedly on meditative equipoise,
one purifies the three karmas through this; thus, siddhi swiftly manifests before one,
sustained by the power of the Noble Ones and because one's conduct and aspirations are in accord.
All those who delight in cultivation, Who receive and learn from their teachers,
And uphold the transmitted teachings of the Vidyādharas, Without transgressing the samaya,
Exerting themselves without interruption, Free from the hindrances and the intoxication of defilements—
Practicing in accordance with the precepts, Siddhi is accomplished according to one's capacity.
Relying upon the teachings of Mahāvairocana, I briefly demonstrate the practice of yoga;
Through this cultivation and realization of supreme merit, May all sentient beings be universally nourished.
A Single Fascicle of the Method for the Practice of Recitation as Briefly Summarized from the Mahāvairocana Sūtra.
